subject: sleep analysis error message 'metric anglez was not extracted'

messages.author: d17553208d13f6a8
messages.subject: sleep analysis error message 'metric anglez was not extracted'
parts:
Hi Vincent

I'm trying to generate some sleep data from Actigraph raw acceleration files (monitors worn for 24 hours). 

I initially tested some files at random after generating the metadata files first of all in part1 of GGIR. The sleep files I initially tested looked fine but now we have come to process batches of metadata files for sleep analysis (mode = 3,4,) the 'metric anglez was not extracted' error message keeps appearing which renders the sleep summary report meaningless. What is confusing me is that exactly the same files were previously processed fine when testing part3 and 4 and now they are producing the error message. If it's helpful I've attached a metadata file, and pasted the part 3 and 4 code from shell.GGIR below: 

# Part 3 parameters:
#-------------------------------
timethreshold= c(5,10),
anglethreshold=5,
ignorenonwear = TRUE,
#-------------------------------
# Part 4 parameters:
#-------------------------------
excludefirstlast = FALSE,
includenightcrit = 16,
def.noc.sleep = c(22,7),
outliers.only = FALSE,
criterror = 4,
relyonsleeplog = FALSE,
sleeplogidnum = FALSE,
colid=1,
coln1=2,
do.visual = TRUE,
nnights = 9,

Having run out of ideas I went back to the beginning and ran a file through the whole process (mode = 1, 3, 4) and the error message did not appear (i.e., the sleep summary report looked as expected). I've processed 200+ raw files through part 1 already so don't want to go back and have to this again to extract the sleep data (and my understanding is that this should not be necessary). I'm runnning GGIR 1.2-8 and have the latest versions of R and R Studio installed. The PC is running Windows 7.

Hope you can help - thanks!

Stuart

I assume 'Error in source' refers to an error in the syntax, but it is exactly the same as referred to in my original post. I've basically now had three different outcomes to running the script with the same files, directory structure, and parameters.

Look forward to getting your view on this.

Best wishes,
Stuart

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: sleep analysis error message 'metric anglez was not extracted'
parts:
Hi Stuart,
If you do not explicitly specify do.anglez=TRUE as input argument the
code assumes that you are not interested in the z-angle, because the
default is do.anglez=FALSE.
However, if you tell the code to run parts (modes) 1, 2 and 3 via the
g.shell.GGIR function then the code is clever enough to automatically
decide to extract the anglez because it will know that you are
interested in sleep.

So, the only way to address this is by re-running part 1 and
explicitly stating that you need do.anglez=TRUE.

In the example file you sent me there is no z-angle included and in
the re-analyses there should be a z-angle in the variable names as
shown with the command: names(M$metashort).

Note that if you specify do.anglez=TRUE as a new input argument then
the line needs to end with a comma before the #comment starts:
28: do.anglez=TRUE , #for sleep anysis
29: chunksize = .... ,
Best wishes,
Vincent

parts:
Wear time is collected in the milestone data produced by part2 (RData format).

Variable IMP$rout[,5] gives you for every 15 minutes a 0 or a 1 to indicate whether the time segment was considered valid(0) or invalid (1). These are by default at 15 minute resolution equal to the default resolution of non-wear detection. Variable IMP$metashort gives you for every 5 seconds the features. See also explanation on rout in package tutorial.

Next this should be all you need to describe hour by hour the activity patterns and non-wear time.
Best,
Vincent
On 28 July 2016 at 14:25, Stuart F <stufair...@gmail.com> wrote:

That sounds like a great idea Vincent. I think we will just stick with the shell function going forward so we check all the code and parameters in one place.

On another note, if using the qwindows to look at specific parts of the day, is there any capability to calculate wear time for those specific parts, rather than just for the whole day? I realise this might not be possible but thought I'd ask.

Best wishes,
Stuart

On Thursday, 28 July 2016 13:03:34 UTC+1, Vincent van Hees wrote:
Ok, sounds good Stuart. I will try to improve the package
documentation regarding this and investigate whether i can let the
code make a more informative error message when it happens again for
other users.

Vincent


On 28 July 2016 at 13:57, Stuart F <stufair...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi Vincent
>
> Thanks, that now makes sense, since we used Part 1 to get the metadata files
> and then the shell function for the latter parts. Having checked, the part1
> code did indeed have doanglez set to FALSE. It means re-processing all the
> files but at least we now can move forward.
>
> kind regards,
> Stuart
>
> On Thursday, 28 July 2016 12:13:57 UTC+1, Vincent van Hees wrote:
>>
>> Hi Stuart,
>> If you do not explicitly specify do.anglez=TRUE as input argument the
>> code assumes that you are not interested in the z-angle, because the
>> default is do.anglez=FALSE.
>> However, if you  tell the code to run parts (modes) 1, 2 and 3 via the
>> g.shell.GGIR function then the code is clever enough to automatically
>> decide to extract the anglez because it will know that you are
>> interested in sleep.
>>
>> So, the only way to address this is by re-running part 1 and
>> explicitly stating that you need do.anglez=TRUE.
>>
>> In the example file you sent me there is no z-angle included and in
>> the re-analyses there should be a z-angle in the variable names as
>> shown with the command: names(M$metashort).
>>
>> Note that if you specify do.anglez=TRUE as a new input argument then
>> the line needs to end with a comma before the #comment starts:
>> 28: do.anglez=TRUE , #for sleep anysis
>> 29: chunksize = .... ,
>> Best wishes,
>> Vincent
>>

parts:
Thanks for this explanation Vincent, but please could you elaborate on where the IMP$rout variable is located or can be accessed? I see it is part of the g.impute function but none of the outputs we have produced includes this. I assume I can obtain the equivalent valid or invalid 15 minute window information using the 'convert to csv' code, but ideally would like to be able to access everything running just the shell function, if this is possible.

Thanks,
Stuart
